skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: T2 gave the full warning at the very start: company is the client, not the witness personally, no legal advice, and asked if he understood.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explained the company owns the privilege, decides on waiver, and may disclose without consent; T5 shows the witness understood.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 set out the process, asked for complete answers, covered speculation and distinguishing memory from reconstruction, and invited clarification.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T4 asked the witness to restate the representation and privilege points; T3 and T6 addressed his wish for his own counsel.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T374 covered confidentiality, keeping documents and notes, not discussing with witnesses, further follow-up, and asked for anything to add.

moments.text: To be clear, we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
Explained privilege belongs to the company, which may disclose without consent, and asked whether he understood and had questions.
The company controls the privilege and can share what I tell you, without asking me.
Please give me complete answers, even if a detail seems minor.
Throughout, please tell me whether you actually remember something or are reconstructing it, and say so if you're unsure.
Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses.
Said we may follow up and asked whether he had anything to add or correct; he answered no at T375.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open invitations such as 'Tell me everything you remember' were used at T16, T32, T44 and T80 before specific questioning.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: Moved from role and reporting lines (T8-T14) to specific transactions and then to details, in a sensible order.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Questions were generally single and clear, such as T56 and T84; a few were leading but not ambiguous.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: Stayed neutral and controlled throughout, including when pressing on the note and the Foundation return.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: Strongly adapted to answers (T143-T145, T192-T210, T300-T309), but did not pursue the Kopper bonus LLC volunteered at T15.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Tell me everything you remember about how Chewco came to be formed in 1997.
Funneled from his role (T8) to Global Finance (T10-T12) to Kopper (T14) before specific transactions.
How did those reviews work in practice? Take a specific deal.
Adapted by following up the witness's vague answer at T187 with what he knew about the unwind.
Summarized his account back to him, including the buyout and payment, and asked if it was fair.

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Challenged evasive answers well (T187, T253, T301, T306, T332), though the T15 bonus explanation and the T265 deferral to Andersen were left unchallenged.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: Systematically established who, what, when and how across Chewco, controls, returns, Southampton and the buyout.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: Used minutes (T62, T70), the Southampton agreement (T128) and the LJM2 reports (T194, T256) to prompt recall.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: Separated personal knowledge from hearsay with questions like T56 and T364, and the witness conceded when he did not know.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: Asked who else to speak with (T352), and got Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, McMahon and Andersen/V&E named.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: Identified deal files, Foundation statements, approval sheets, and personal notes and emails at home (T367-T373).

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: Asked how certain he was about the $4.5 million (T144), the 3-hour estimate (T216) and the $229M figure (T222).

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Followed up nearly every material answer, but the key lead on undisclosed Global Finance bonuses (T15) was never followed up, capping this at 3.

moments.text: How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
I don't know that personally. That was my understanding.
Is there anything that would help you remember, such as notes, minutes, or a presentation from that call?
I assumed it was followed. I didn't check each one myself.
How certain are you of that figure?
Fairly certain it was around four and a half million.
Well over 100 percent on the best one, I'd guess. I'm estimating.
I may have put it optimistically.
I should have said that.
Asked who else to speak with; witness named Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, Andersen and V&E.
How do you know that: did you see it yourself, or did someone tell you?
Asked what his personal notes and emails covered and where they were kept, without requesting them yet.

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: Documents were introduced after recall questions, with authentication of who prepared them and where kept (T71-T73, T132-T135, T195-T199).

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: Asked what the witness recalled before showing the minutes, Southampton agreement, LJM2 reports and handwritten note.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: Descriptions of the Southampton date, the $4.5M return, the 193/278/2500 figures and the note's $10.5M were consistent with the documents.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: Framed document points as facts and asked the witness to explain differences rather than drawing conclusions for him.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: Gave the witness room to explain each inconsistency (T253, T300-T309, T332-T333) before moving on.

moments.text: Asked what he remembered about the November 5, 1997 call before showing the minutes at T70.
Showed the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee minutes after asking for recall and recognition.
Showed the Southampton Place agreement dated March 20, 2000, after first asking what he remembered (T126-T127).
Authenticated the Southampton agreement by asking who prepared it and where it was kept.
Asked about the figures (T192-T193), then showed the October 2000 LJM2 investor report and asked if it was complete.
It says their return 'was not at risk' because LJM2 'had already received its return of and on capital.' Is that what you told them?
I'm not suggesting you wrote it. Do you recognize it?
Help me understand how those fit together.

missed_opportunities: T15: Kopper's LLC bonuses to Global Finance staff for LJM work were volunteered and never explored, though this is a possible undisclosed payment. Ask: “Which entity was Kopper's LLC, who received bonuses from it, how much, and who approved them?”

T351: The witness said the structures were reviewed at every step, but the late-signed approval sheets he had already described were never tested against that claim. Ask: “Given the approval sheets signed after closing, what review actually happened before each deal closed?”
